title: `MODE`: ties go to the value seen first, in the order DuckDB reads the rows
verdict: ties are the engine's without ORDER BY; with one, the first in that order
description: `MODE(x)` counts each non-NULL value and keeps, of the most frequent, the one whose first row came first (`first_row`). Without an `ORDER BY` that is the order in which threads read and merge the rows, so ties depend on parallelism: on 3,000,000 rows alternating 5 and 3, starting with 5, `MODE(x)` gave 3. With `MODE(x ORDER BY …)` the rows arrive sorted, and the first of the tied values in that order wins: `MODE(x ORDER BY x)` is the smallest, `ORDER BY x DESC` the largest. `mode() WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY x)` is the same. NULLs are skipped; no values give NULL. `-0.0` and `0.0` count as one value.
The docs are silent on the first-occurrence tie rule: a docs gap.
reference: `AggFn.mode` (`modeOf`, #53): the most frequent value, and of the values that tie, the first in the measure's sort order (rows that tie on it in list order). The parser refuses `MODE` without an order; Ibis's `mode()` becomes `MODE(x ORDER BY x)`. `Rel.windowsTotal` reports a mode as the engine's choice unless the sort includes its argument's column or the group's and the order's columns contain a key.

evidence.sql: SELECT mode(x ORDER BY x), mode(x ORDER BY x DESC), mode(x ORDER BY i DESC), mode(x) FROM (SELECT CASE WHEN i % 2 = 0 THEN 5 ELSE 3 END AS x, i FROM range(3000000) t(i))
SELECT mode() WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY x DESC), mode() WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY x) FROM (VALUES (1), (3), (3), (1)) t(x)
SELECT mode(x ORDER BY y) FROM (VALUES (1, 2), (3, 1), (3, 3), (1, 0)) t(x, y)

evidence.note: Execute records first_row as the state's own count; Combine keeps the min of two states' local positions, so parallel ties follow thread order
mode: affected by ordering; tie rule not stated
threads=4: mode(v ORDER BY ord) of tied 'z' (1), 'y' (2) → z; DESC → y
an unordered tie may return either candidate
ordered ties keep the first value under the full order (NULLS FIRST/LAST) → b, a, b
